title: Multivalent lamin binding controls the meshwork structure in a self-assembled model of the nuclear lamina
authors: Hadiya Abdul Hameed; Ata Utku Ozkan; Aykut Erbas
one_liner_zh: 该文用聚合物物理模型模拟核纤层蛋白自组装网络，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作边缘（核膜/染色质相关），但核心是蛋白-蛋白相互作用，无TF-DNA结合或AI/物理模拟方法，仅间接相关。
abstract: The nuclear lamina is a specialized two-dimensional filamentous polymer meshwork that provides structural integrity and elasticity to the nucleus while orchestrating diverse cellular processes. Composed of interacting A- and B-type lamin networks, this structure undergoes tightly regulated self-assembly that is frequently perturbed by disease-causing mutations such as those observed in laminopathies or cardiomyopathies. However, because filament assembly, peripheral adsorption of lamins, and network branching occur concurrently in vivo , isolating the specific biophysical parameters that dictate emergent lamina topology has remained a major challenge. Here, we present a polymer-physics approach that explicitly resolves the spontaneous self-assembly of lamin networks under nuclear confinement. By modeling lamin dimers as semiflexible filaments with distinct interactive domains, we demonstrate that the formation of continuous, high-aspect-ratio fibers strictly requires a coordination cascade of parallel lateral alignment sites and longitudinal head-to-tail interactions between lamins. We show that the thermodynamic affinity between lamin-A and the peripheral boundary (i.e., the inner nuclear membrane and lamin B network) acts as a kinetic switch: weak surface adsorption drives network phase separation and large lamin-free gaps, whereas robust substrate binding stabilizes highly branched networks with uniform lamin distribution. Finally, uniaxial compression simulations reveal that mutations altering these molecular binding interfaces severely compromise macroscale nuclear load-bearing capacity and induce structural vulnerabilities. Collectively, our model establishes a predictive, multi-scale view that directly bridges nanoscale lamin interactions with mesoscale topological remodeling of lamina and macroscale nuclear mechanopathology.
abstract_zh: 核纤层是一种特化的二维丝状聚合物网络，为细胞核提供结构完整性和弹性，同时协调多种细胞过程。它由相互作用的A型和B型lamin网络组成，其结构经历严格调控的自组装，而这种自组装常因致病突变（如laminopathies或心肌病中观察到的突变）而受到干扰。然而，由于丝状组装、lamin的外周吸附以及网络分支在体内同时发生，因此分离决定lamin网络涌现拓扑结构的具体生物物理参数一直是一项重大挑战。在此，我们提出一种聚合物物理学方法，明确解析核约束下lamin网络的自发自组装。通过将lamin二聚体建模为具有不同相互作用结构域的半柔性丝状体，我们证明连续高长径比纤维的形成严格依赖于lamin之间平行侧向排列位点和纵向头尾相互作用的协调级联。我们表明，lamin-A与外围边界（即内核膜和lamin B网络）之间的热力学亲和力充当动力学开关：弱表面吸附驱动网络相分离 (phase separation) 并产生大的lamin缺失间隙，而强底物结合则稳定高度分支且lamin分布均匀的网络。最后，单轴压缩模拟揭示，改变这些分子结合界面的突变严重损害宏观核承载能力并诱导结构脆弱性。总体而言，我们的模型建立了一个预测性的多尺度视角，直接将纳米尺度的lamin相互作用与中尺度的lamin网络拓扑重塑及宏观的核力学病理学联系起来。
